service.name: Daytime live music and sound baths
service.serviceType: Live music and sound baths during the day for senior living communities, memorial services, brunches, workplaces, yoga studios, farmers markets, libraries and rec centers
service.description: Solo musicians, duos and a sound bath for daytime bookings across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor: a jazz duo for senior living and memory care, a guitarist or pianist for a funeral or memorial service, live music for Sunday brunch, a daytime sound bath for studios, offices, senior centers and schools, and musicians for farmers markets, libraries and rec center programs, on one contract with sound included.

faqs.q: Do you book live music during the day, on weekdays?
faqs.a: Yes. A weekday afternoon at a senior living community, a lunchtime sound bath at an office, a weekday morning memorial service and a Saturday farmers market are all bookings we take, usually a solo or a duo. Send the date and the venue and we'll come back with a recommendation and a price. Signet Artists books daytime music across Denver and the Front Range.

Solo and duo, almost always: one musician with a guitar or a piano, or upright bass and guitar, at the level of a conversation and in a corner with no stage. In a small space the guitar plays without amplification at all. A trio plays a brunch or a community evening where the space is bigger, and the sound bath is one facilitator.

faqs.q: What does a daytime venue need?
faqs.a: A solo sets up in about 6 by 4 feet and a duo in 8 by 6, on the floor, with one dedicated 20-amp circuit; outdoors with no power, a guitarist plays on a battery-powered system. Setup is 45 minutes for a solo and an hour for a duo, before the program starts, and packing up takes 30 to 45 minutes. A sound bath needs enough floor for everyone to lie down and sets up about ninety minutes ahead of doors. Sets run 45 to 60 minutes with music through the breaks.

faqs.q: Can we book the same act every month?
faqs.a: Yes. A standing date, monthly or every other week, runs on one contract with one personal contact for the whole run. A community that books the jazz duo gets upright bass and guitar playing the standards on every visit, and a named act, Tejas Singh or Firstwater, is the same act on every date.

faqs.q: Do you provide the vendor paperwork a facility or a city needs?
faqs.a: Yes. A certificate of insurance naming your venue as additional insured, a W-9 and one itemized invoice come in the same email as the contract, which is usually what a business office needs to set up a vendor before the first date.

faqs.q: Do you play outdoors, at a market or in a park?
faqs.a: Yes, on three conditions written down before the day: a covered, level and dry performance area, power run to it or a battery-powered system agreed in advance, and a rain call agreed with the coordinator, because Colorado weather changes fast.

faqs.q: How much does daytime live music cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the size, the length and the date, and we publish no prices of our own. What live music costs in this market, with the source for each figure, is on the pricing page, and each date or run of dates is priced as its own job.
